paras: The killing of Lovels Green and Mrs. Alguire was a double homicide at Grand Haven, Michigan, on the night of about August 14, 1881, in which John Allguire shot Green, a Black man who had lived for several years with Allguire's white mother, and his mother also died. Allguire surrendered and claimed self-defence, but a coroner's jury found that he had killed both. Newspapers from New York to Virginia carried the story, stressing that the dead man was 'colored' and the woman white.

Green, called Frederick in the Detroit wire report and Lovels or Loveloss in Michigan dispatches, had lived for several years at Grand Haven with Allguire's mother. The Richmond Dispatch identified Allguire, aged 23, as 'a Frenchman' and added that his mother 'has served a couple of terms in the House of Correction for disorderly conduct.'

On the night of the killing Allguire gave himself up to the sheriff at Grand Haven, saying he had just shot Green. In his first account, carried by a Detroit dispatch, Green had quarreled with his mother, struck her on the head with a gun and attacked Allguire, who fired in self-defence. The top of Green's head was blown off, and the mother, found dead in the same room, had a fractured skull.

A Grand Haven dispatch gave a different version of Allguire's claim, that Green had shot his mother before Allguire shot Green, but noted that 'no bullet-wounds are on her body.' The same dispatch said the evidence against Allguire was 'entirely circumstantial' and that 'He threatened to kill both.'

A coroner's inquest heard evidence over both bodies on August 15, and the next morning the jury returned a verdict that Allguire killed both his mother and Green. According to the verdict, Green was shot in the head with a shotgun and the mother was killed by a blow to the back of the head with the stock of the gun, which was broken. No report of an indictment or trial appears in the coverage through September 1881.

The story reached national readers through a Detroit wire report that the New-York Tribune headed 'KILLING HIS MOTHER'S LOVER' and that repeated Allguire's self-defence account without comment. The Chicago Tribune ran its own Grand Haven dispatches, 'THE GRAND HAVEN TRAGEDY' and 'THE GRAND HAVEN MURDER', which set Allguire's claim against the physical evidence and reported the verdict.

Other papers put the interracial household at the center of the story. The Richmond Dispatch, under 'Terrible Result of a Horrid Crime', called the mother Green's 'mistress', noted her jail terms and said Allguire 'has a fair reputation considering his surroundings,' while the Cambria Freeman of Pennsylvania ended its two-sentence item with 'She is a white woman.' Michigan weeklies, the Lake County Star and the Owosso Times, ran the same news column a week later, calling Green 'his mother's paramour' and printing the coroner's verdict.

Accounts of the mother's death differ: Allguire said in one version that Green struck her with a gun and in another that Green shot her, while the coroner's jury, after the inquest found no bullet wounds, held that Allguire killed her with the gun stock. The Michigan column said Allguire claimed to have killed Green 'in revenge' rather than in self-defence, and the Cambria Freeman dated the shooting to 'Monday last' rather than the night of August 14 given in the first dispatches.

reader.title: Killing of Lovels Green and Mrs. Alguire
bases: All reports describe a killing by one man, John Allguire, of his mother and her Black companion in a household quarrel, with no mob, crowd or band and no stated racial motive (A1, A2, A3, A6).

A Detroit wire report (A1, A4) and separate Grand Haven dispatches to the Chicago Tribune (A2, A3) agree that Allguire killed Green and that his mother died the same night; the Michigan column (A6) repeats the coroner's verdict.

accounts.label: Allguire's statement (Detroit wire)
accounts.gist: Green quarreled with Allguire's mother, struck her on the head with a gun and attacked Allguire, who shot Green in self-defence; the mother's skull was fractured by Green's blow.

accounts.label: Allguire's statement (Grand Haven dispatch and Michigan column)
accounts.gist: Green shot the mother first, and Allguire then shot Green, 'in revenge' according to the Michigan column.

accounts.label: Coroner's jury
accounts.gist: On circumstantial evidence, including the absence of bullet wounds on the mother, the jury found that Alguire killed both, Green by shotgun and his mother by a blow with the gun stock.

framing.detail: The Detroit wire ran under 'KILLING HIS MOTHER'S LOVER' and gave Allguire's self-defence account without comment.
The Chicago Tribune's Grand Haven dispatches, 'THE GRAND HAVEN TRAGEDY' and 'THE GRAND HAVEN MURDER', set Allguire's claim against the physical evidence and reported the verdict against him.

The Richmond Dispatch headed the wire 'Terrible Result of a Horrid Crime', stressed the mother was 'a white woman' with jail terms, and said Allguire 'has a fair reputation considering his surroundings.'
The Cambria Freeman reduced the story to two sentences ending 'She is a white woman.'

conflicts.note: The Detroit wire used Frederick; the Grand Haven dispatch and the Michigan column used Loveloss/Lovels.
